sections.heading: Choose an online basketball training format with a clear next step
sections.text: A lesson library, a scheduled remote session and a workout-tracking app ask different things of a player. Before starting, identify the activity, the equipment and whether anyone will review your recording. Jr. NBA provides an official instructional curriculum and practice resources; follow the instructions for the activity you choose. Write one question you want to revisit after the session so your recording has a purpose.

sections.heading: Build a useful practice video record
sections.text: Keep a simple session note beside the original file: date, activity, camera position and the part you want to review. If an instructor requests an angle or an unedited sequence, record that first. For a shooting clip, choose a position that keeps the player, basketball and basket visible throughout the attempt.

subsections.heading: Keep attempts in their original order
subsections.text: Save the complete sequence before picking a favorite. A short highlight can sit beside the full session, with its start time in the filename or notes so you can find the surrounding attempts again.

sections.heading: Add a shot tracer to a practice highlight
sections.text: Choose a visible attempt from your own footage and import it into the tool above. Select a range of up to 30 seconds that includes the release and finish. Watch whether the trail follows the intended basketball, especially when another player crosses the frame. Export an edited copy after checking the preview.

subsections.heading: Send the right version for the purpose
subsections.text: Use the original when discussing the recording with an instructor, and the traced copy when you want to share the flight of a favorite shot. Give each file a clear name so the two versions remain easy to identify.

faq: Does HoopCut provide online basketball lessons?
HoopCut is a video-editing tool. Choose instruction separately, then use this page to add a tracer to a practice recording you already have.
What should I record for a remote coach?
Ask the coach for their required view, duration and file format. Preserve that recording before making a short edited version.
Can a tracer tell me whether my technique improved?
A tracer visualizes the ball in a clip. It does not provide a technique assessment or prove improvement between sessions.
What if my training session is longer than 30 seconds?
Keep the full recording separately and select a range of up to 30 seconds for this web tool.
Can I share the exported clip?
You can download the free Firework version and share it through your chosen app, with the lesson or session context you want viewers to understand.

subsections.heading: Keep game time and file time separate

faq: Does this page record a live basketball game?

Can I upload an entire game?
The upload limit is 512 MB, and each web result covers up to 30 seconds. Prepare a smaller source excerpt if the game file exceeds the upload limit.
Should I zoom in on the shooter?
Check that your framing still contains the ball’s complete flight and the basket. Choose the view that preserves the sequence you want to show.
Does the recorder need to be HoopCut?
You can start with your own saved basketball footage. The web upload accepts MP4, MOV and WebM files; preview the result to confirm your file works.
Will a tracer fix a blocked recording?
The visual effect cannot restore action that was hidden or outside the frame. Try a clearer recording or select another attempt.

sections.heading: A published example: the NBA 2026 three-point contest
sections.text: The official 2026 rules gave each shooter 70 seconds for 27 balls. Four racks held four one-point balls and a two-point money ball; the fifth held five two-point balls. Two additional blue balls were worth three points each. The possible total was 40. The three highest first-round scores advanced to the final. This is a dated NBA contest format, not a universal rule for every shooting challenge.

sections.heading: Write a complete rule sheet for your own shootout
sections.text: Agree on your format before starting. Decide how many positions and attempts you will use, which balls are worth extra points, when the clock starts and what happens in a tie. Give everyone the same sheet and keep it beside the score record. Refer to the official event document when reproducing a particular competition.

subsections.heading: Keep attempt order visible in the recording
subsections.text: Frame the shooting positions and retain the continuous round, even if you later share just one make. Number the attempts in your notes so a short export can be matched back to the correct place in the sequence.

steps: Record the event or house-rule version and its date.

sections.heading: Add a shot tracer to one shootout highlight
sections.text: Choose an attempt with the release and hoop clearly visible. Keep the location recognizable so the clip makes sense alongside your scoring notes. Select up to 30 seconds in the tool, inspect the trail and export Firework. When sharing, describe the format you actually played rather than borrowing a score label from another event.

subsections.heading: Keep the round and highlight as separate files
subsections.text: An edited clip can draw attention to one ball flight, while the complete recording preserves the sequence. Give both files the same round identifier and add the attempt number to the highlight.

faq: Does every 3-point shootout use NBA contest rules?
No. Check the organizer’s published format or agree on a written format with the people playing.
Are contest points the same as a normal game basket?
A shootout assigns points according to its own format. Use the playing rules for a regulation game and the event rules for a contest.
Where can I check the NBA example on this page?
The source below is the official 2026 State Farm 3-Point Contest rules PDF. Check a newer event’s document when following a different year.
Can HoopCut keep score or decide a disputed attempt?
No. The tool adds a visual shot trail. Retain your score sheet and complete original footage for any scoring review.
Can I export the complete shootout?
The web tool processes up to 30 seconds at a time. Keep the full round and choose an individual sequence for the tracer highlight.

description: Learn how a legal full-court shot is scored under NBA rules, keep the play’s context and add a shot tracer to your own recorded attempt with HoopCut.
heading: How many points is a full-court shot? Trace the play after checking the rule
intro: Under NBA rules, a legal made full-court field goal at the basket your team is attacking is worth three points. Extra distance does not add a bonus. Use HoopCut to add a tracer to your own recorded attempt while keeping the original.

sections.heading: Full-court shot scoring under NBA playing rules
sections.text: NBA Rule 5 values a legal made field goal outside the offensive three-point line at three points. The distance beyond that line does not create a four-point or five-point basket. A long attempt still has to be legal and count as a field goal. A special exhibition or local shooting contest may set different point values, so identify the rule set before labeling the clip.

sections.heading: Keep the release and result in your recording
sections.text: A long flight may move far beyond a camera view chosen only for the shooter. Check that your view includes the release, ball flight and far basket. Keep the full original sequence. If the video is being used to discuss a live-game call, retain any available clock and surrounding action as well.

subsections.heading: Separate what is visible from what you infer
subsections.text: Write down which details the recording actually shows. If the release, foot position or clock is out of view, preserve that uncertainty in your description rather than treating the edited highlight as proof of the missing detail.

steps: Identify whether the clip comes from a game, practice or contest.
Keep the complete attempt and any visible timing context.
Note the source timestamp before creating a short copy.

sections.heading: Use a tracer to highlight a visible long-range flight
sections.text: Import your saved basketball clip and select up to 30 seconds. Follow the preview from release through the middle of the flight to the basket. A distant ball can become small, blurred or hidden, so choose another recording if the trail does not follow it clearly. The shared sample shows the effect on ordinary basketball footage; it is not evidence of a full-court make.

subsections.heading: Describe the attempt accurately when sharing
subsections.text: Pair the edited file with a caption that identifies the session and the outcome visible in the original. Keep the original linked in your own notes to retain the surrounding play.

faq: Is a made full-court shot worth four points in the NBA?
No. A legal made field goal from that distance is worth three points under NBA Rule 5.
Does this answer cover every basketball competition?
This page states the NBA rule. Check the rules for your own league, exhibition or shooting challenge before applying a point value.
Can the tracer confirm whether the basket should count?
No. It adds a visual trail. It does not officiate timing, foot position, violations or scoring.
What if the ball disappears halfway through the clip?
Try a clearer source angle or another attempt. A tracer cannot recover a reliable view of a ball that is missing from the recording.
Can I try the effect on a shorter shot?
Yes. Upload your own clear basketball recording, choose up to 30 seconds and preview or export Firework free.
